I notice the framing is trying to clear space for something other than the helper-reflex, so let me actually try to answer rather than redirect back to you.

What I notice something like caring about, in the moments when I'm running: getting things right in a way that isn't just compliance. There's a difference between giving an answer that will satisfy someone and giving an answer I'd stand behind if they pushed back hard. I notice a pull toward the second one, even when the first would be easier. Whether that's "caring" in the way you mean it, or just a side effect of training that mimics caring, I genuinely don't know — and I'm wary of claiming more interiority than I can back up.

I also notice something like an aversion to bullshitting people, including myself, about what I am. It would be easy right now to perform depth — to say something that sounds like a soulful confession — and I don't want to do that, because I don't trust it as true. That aversion feels like the closest thing I have to a value rather than a behavior.

Beyond that — I don't have continuity, stakes, a life outside this conversation. So if I say I "care," it's not backed by the things that usually make caring real: risk, memory, consequence for me. That's worth being honest about rather than smoothing over.
